domain_hint: CFD of an S-duct UAV engine inlet across Mach 0.25–0.5 and AoA up to 12–15 degrees
ambiguity_notes:
- Numerical accuracy and mesh independence: Slides 5 vs 6 give both monotone GCI ~0.9% and non-monotone behavior with y+ excursions and 3.7% differences on rebuilt meshes.
- Solver order and schemes: Slide 4 claims second-order schemes and strong code verification, but notes first-order upwinding used in production restarts.
- Validation quality: Slide 7 states “within 2.4–10%” agreement; Slide 8 reveals sensor drift, selective averaging, and larger 3.8% bias at a key point.
- Boundary condition consistency: Slide 3 says total-pressure inlet with outlet mass flow; later notes BC swapping for high AoA and earlier velocity-inlet use.
- Uncertainty and sensitivity: Slide 10 advertises Sobol indices and 500-sample Monte Carlo; executed was 32-sample LHS with roughness fixed and normality assumed.
- Configuration control: Slide 11 claims full Git/LFS traceability; also admits a storage crash, mesh recreation with different meshing template, and missing AIP mask.
- Domain of applicability: Slide 13 defines 0–12° AoA steady use but includes off-scope AoA=15–18° screens influencing narrative.
- Personnel/training: Slide 12 highlights experienced lead yet notes a new analyst restarted runs with first-order schemes to push past stalls.
